chunks: Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shazaan, and Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Safwan ibn Yahya from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the light sleep (khafqah) and the two light sleeps (khafqatan), so he (peace be upon him) said: 'I do not know what is the light sleep and the two light sleeps. Indeed, Allah says: 'But! The human being has an insight unto himself.' Indeed, Ali (peace be upon him) was saying: 'The one who finds the taste of sleep while standing, or sitting, so the Wudu is Obligated upon him.'

key_terms.طَعْمَ النَّوْمِ: The taste of sleep (a state of drowsiness where one is aware but not fully asleep)

ai.seo_question: Does light sleep while standing or sitting break Wudu according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi clarifies the jurisprudential threshold for nullifying ablution (Wudu) by distinguishing between dozing and deep sleep. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) anchors the ruling in the Prophetic tradition of Imam Ali (AS), defining the 'taste of sleep' as the point where sensory awareness of the body's position is lost, thereby requiring renewal of Wudu. This establishes a practical standard for worshippers to determine when their ritual purity is broken during prayer or recitation.
